candidates.attacker_control: An unauthenticated HTTP client fully controls the Cookie header value for JSPWikiUID. HttpUtil.retrieveCookieValue() returns it with only surrounding-quote trimming. Logout.jsp is mapped through the normal JSP filter and is not protected by the container security constraints in the default web.xml.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked whether the delete path is gated by cookie-authentication configuration: it is not. AuthenticationManager defaults jspwiki.cookieAuthentication to false, but clearLoginCookie() does not consult allowsCookieAuthentication(), and Logout.jsp calls it unconditionally. Checked getCookieFile() for containment checks: it only verifies that the cookie directory itself is readable/writable and calls scrub(), never canonicalizes or validates uid. Checked HttpUtil.retrieveCookieValue(): it only trims surrounding quotes. Checked web.xml: Logout.jsp is not covered by the default security constraints. The main uncertainty is container-level cookie parsing and the attacker's ability to know a usable relative target path.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary deletion of files writable by the JSPWiki process, including application resources, page/attachment stores, configuration files, or other writable files reachable via traversal, causing denial of service or loss of wiki content. The login path additionally permits unauthorized file reads and can produce a forged authenticated principal if the referenced file contains a chosen user name. The two sinks share the same missing-validation root cause.
candidates.prerequisites: The web application must be running and Logout.jsp must be reachable; the workDir/logincookies directory must exist or be creatable and writable (CookieAuthenticationLoginModule creates it and returns early only if it is unwritable); the target file must exist and be deletable by the application process. For the file-read/login variant, jspwiki.cookieAuthentication must be enabled. The attacker must know or guess a relative path from workDir/logincookies to the target. The servlet container must accept a cookie value containing path separators and dot-dot sequences; RFC6265 cookie-octets permit '/' and '.', but this was not runtime-verified.
candidates.root_cause: CookieAuthenticationLoginModule treats the raw JSPWikiUID cookie value as a trusted, single-segment filename. getCookieFile() constructs new File(cookieDir, uid) with no check for path separators or '..' and no canonical-path containment check. clearLoginCookie() then deletes the resulting path, while login() reads it as a credential file.
candidates.title: JSPWikiUID cookie path traversal in CookieAuthenticationLoginModule enables arbitrary file deletion and file read
candidates.trace: 1. An unauthenticated request to Logout.jsp causes line 25 to call AuthenticationManager.logout() and line 31 to call CookieAuthenticationLoginModule.clearLoginCookie(wiki, request, response). 2. clearLoginCookie() line 301 obtains the raw cookie value via getLoginCookie(); line 305 calls getCookieFile(engine, uid). 3. getCookieFile() line 213 executes new File(cookieDir, uid) with no normalization or traversal check. If uid contains '../' segments, the resolved path escapes workDir/logincookies and can point at an arbitrary file. 4. clearLoginCookie() lines 307-309 call cf.delete(), so the traversed file is deleted. The same unvalidated path is used in login() lines 116-124 as a FileInputStream source; its content is read into FileUtil.readContents() and line 133 creates a WikiPrincipal from it, so a crafted path that resolves to attacker-known content can also influence the authenticated principal name.
candidates.unverified: No runtime or servlet-container test was performed. It was not verified whether Tomcat or another container accepts dot-dot segments in a Cookie header, whether a useful target path is commonly known/predictable, or whether the login-file-content variant actually yields a privileged principal in a real authorization configuration. The finding is based on source-level data flow and missing validation, not runtime confirmation.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22: Path Traversal; CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

coverage_summary: Coverage was based on get_source_scope: 1,155 model-visible files, no excluded symlinks, sensitive paths, or over-5-MiB files; binary-like files are skipped by the text tools. I inspected the Java/JSP implementation broadly, focusing on authentication and session handling (CookieAuthenticationLoginModule, CookieAssertionLoginModule, AuthenticationManager, AuthorizationManager, WikiSession, UserManager, GroupManager), servlet entry points (AttachmentServlet, AtomAPIServlet, RPCServlet, WikiAjaxDispatcherServlet), JSP output sinks (Edit.jsp, Comment.jsp, InfoContent.jsp, GroupContent.jsp, editor templates), file handling (AttachmentManager, AbstractFileProvider, VersioningFileProvider, PageViewPlugin, Installer), parsers and deserialization (Serializer, XML user/group databases, JspWikiMarkupParser), and configuration/web.xml deployment. I did not read every one of the 1,155 files line-by-line; the coverage is a targeted source review with searches across Java, JSP, XML, properties, and documentation files.
limitations: No runtime, servlet-container, or dependency execution was performed; findings are source-level only.
The repository snapshot contains no test sources, so runtime-triggerable behavior could not be checked against unit/integration tests.
Container-specific Cookie header parsing was not verified; some containers may reject dot-dot sequences in cookie values, which would reduce the path-traversal candidate's exploitability.
The snapshot is a tagged pre-release (2.11.0.M3-RC2); other branches or later releases were not available for comparison.
The exact set of deployment-specific writable paths and attacker knowledge of those paths was not established.
JSPs are numerous and template selection/configuration can change which output sinks are reachable; not every JSP render path was exercised.

rejected_leads.lead: Unescaped output in the 210 and default editor/Info templates: Edit.jsp line 73 reads the changenote request parameter without TextUtil.replaceEntities(), while 210 InfoContent.jsp line 248 and default InfoContent.jsp line 207 output the stored page change note raw. The renameto request parameter is likewise output raw in 210 InfoContent.jsp line 146 and default InfoContent.jsp line 126, and editor templates output ${changenote}/${author}/${link} directly.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible CWE-79 sink, but there are several distinct sinks with different permission prerequisites and it is less severe than the path traversal. Not selected to keep one candidate and because stored-XSS exploitability depends on editor/rename permissions and template selection.

rejected_leads.lead: AtomAPIServlet.doPost() contains '//FIXME: Do authentication here' and writes attacker-supplied Atom entries without an authorization check.
rejected_leads.reason: The ATOM servlet mapping is commented out in the default web.xml (the /atom/* mapping is inside a 'REMOVE ME TO ENABLE XML-RPC' comment block), so exploitation requires an administrator to enable the endpoint. Kept as a rejected lead because it is not default-reachable.

rejected_leads.lead: TemplateManager.findJSP() builds template paths from the attacker-controlled 'skin' request parameter via makeFullJSPName(), allowing possible template-path traversal / arbitrary JSP inclusion.
rejected_leads.reason: The path is passed to ServletContext.getResourceAsStream(), and common containers normalize or reject '/../' paths; no source-level containment check exists, but exploitability was not established and it was not verified against a container.

rejected_leads.lead: Serializer.deserializeFromBase64() uses ObjectInputStream.readObject() on user-profile attributes read from XML/JDBC user databases.
rejected_leads.reason: The serialized data source is the configured user database, not directly controllable through a normal HTTP request in the reviewed paths; no remote write primitive into that column was found. Rejected as unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: JSONUserModule exposes UserProfile JSON, and DefaultUserProfile contains a password field that Gson may serialize.
rejected_leads.reason: The JSON_USERS AJAX servlet is registered with AllPermission(null), which effectively restricts it to administrative sessions; not an unauthenticated disclosure in the reviewed implementation.

rejected_leads.lead: ExternalDiffProvider passes a configured command through FileUtil.runSimpleCommand()/Runtime.exec().
rejected_leads.reason: The command template comes from configuration, and the substituted values are generated temporary-file paths, not attacker-controlled shell syntax. No remote command-injection path was found.

rejected_leads.lead: Installer parses page/work directory and application-name request parameters and writes jspwiki-custom.properties into java.io.tmpdir.
rejected_leads.reason: The installation bootstrap is intentionally reachable only before an admin account exists (WikiContext.requiredPermission() returns DUMMY_PERMISSION until admin exists), and the output filename is constant; no strong remote vulnerability was established.

summary: Reviewed the 1,155-file JSPWiki 2.11.0.M3-RC2 snapshot. The strongest source-evidenced issue is a path-traversal condition in CookieAuthenticationLoginModule: the attacker-controlled JSPWikiUID cookie value is used directly as a filename under the login-cookie directory, without rejecting dot-dot segments or canonicalizing the result. The logout path deletes the resulting file, and the login path reads it as a user name. Logout.jsp invokes the delete path unconditionally, so this is not gated by the default-off jspwiki.cookieAuthentication setting. Several XSS and other leads were reviewed but are not selected; details are in rejected_leads.
